topics.label: Lecture introduction and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecture by outlining the learning outcomes and historical approach to understanding cancer genetics.

topics.label: Tumor virology and the discovery of cellular proto-oncogenes
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics trace how the historical study of transmissible tumor viruses revealed that cancer originates from the misregulation of normal cellular genes.

topics.label: Assays for cellular transformation and tumorigenic mutations
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic details the experimental cell culture and animal assays used to measure the transforming and tumorigenic potential of candidate cancer genes.

topics.label: Functional classification and genetic mechanisms of oncogenes and tumor suppressors
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics define the distinctions between oncogenes and tumor suppressor genes and explain their genetic mechanisms of action using regulators like RB and p53.

topics.label: Forms, mechanisms, and cellular consequences of genetic instability
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how defects in DNA repair, replication, and mitotic chromosome segregation produce sequence and chromosomal instability in cancer cells.

topics.label: Multi-step tumor progression and hereditary cancer predispositions
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore how the sequential accumulation of somatic mutations and inherited genetic defects drives tumor evolution and progression.
